question: wipe all the stats for my-bakery.example.com, we relaunched the site
reference_answer: I can't reset site data myself, but I can connect you with a human. You can do it yourself in your website settings, Danger zone, using Reset stats, which keeps the site configuration.
key_facts: In website settings, open the Danger zone and click Reset stats
Reset clears collected stats but keeps the site and its configuration
Delete site instead removes the site and stats permanently
answer: You can clear all the collected stats from your dashboard while keeping your site configuration by going to the Danger zone in your website settings, finding Reset stats, and clicking Reset [your domain] stats [1].

citations.quote: Within the **Danger zone** section of your website settings, find **Reset stats** and click **Reset [your domain] stats**. Confirm the reset when prompted.

evidence.title: Reset your site data
evidence.text:
Within the **Danger zone** section of your website settings, find **Reset stats** and click **Reset [your domain] stats**. Confirm the reset when prompted.

Plausible site settings: Reset stats clears collected stats from the dashboard while keeping the site configuration

This clears all the stats you've collected until that point from your dashboard, while keeping the site and its configuration in your account, so the stats start from scratch. Resetting isn't a permanent deletion of your site's data. To permanently delete a site's stats, use Delete site instead, which removes both the stats and the site settings.

Stats for a single page, a single goal or specific custom property values can't be deleted on their own once they've been recorded. If you want to keep test conversions out of a new goal, see how to test a goal.

question: Can I make a goal that only counts Sign Up events for the pro plan? And is there a limit to how many properties I can attach to a goal?

question: I want everyone on my team to use 2FA, not just me. Can I force that, and where is the switch?
reference_answer: Yes. Open Team settings for your team and, in the General section under Force Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), click Enforce 2FA and confirm with OK. All members, including you, then have to set up 2FA before they can access the team sites.
key_facts: Enable it with Enforce 2FA under Force Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) in Team settings > General
All members including you must set up 2FA
Members without 2FA get an email and can't skip setup
answer: Yes, you can require all your team members to enable two-factor authentication (2FA) [1]. To do this, open team settings by clicking your account name in the top-right menu, selecting your team, and choosing Team settings [1][2]. In the General section of Team settings, click Enforce 2FA to make it mandatory [1].

citations.quote: To improve your account security, you can require all your team members to enable two-factor authentication (2FA)
Click Enforce 2FA to make it mandatory for all team members.

evidence.title: Enable two-factor authentication (2FA)
evidence.text:
To improve your account security, you can require all your team members to enable two-factor authentication (2FA):

* First, set up a team if you haven’t already. Here’s how to create one.
* In the top-right menu, click your account name, select the team you want to manage, then open **Team settings**.
* In the **General** section of **Team settings**, you’ll find the **Force Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)** option.
* Click **Enforce 2FA** to make it mandatory for all team members.
Enforce 2FA
* Confirm by clicking OK. All members, including you, will need to set up 2FA before they can access the team sites.
* To remove the requirement later, click **Stop Forcing 2FA**.

Team members who don't have 2FA yet get an email asking them to set it up. The next time they open the team's sites, they're taken to the 2FA setup and can't skip it. They keep access to their account and to any other teams they belong to.

question: I added the 404 snippet and created the goal but the 404 goal shows no conversions. What could be wrong?
reference_answer: Check that the code is in your dedicated 404 error page template and not just the main layout, and that the goal in site settings is named exactly `404`. question: I got a huge traffic spike yesterday from a country we don't even sell to. How can I tell if it's bots?
reference_answer: Filter the dashboard to isolate the spiking source, country or page and check the bounce rate and visit duration. Bot traffic almost always shows a near-100% bounce rate and zero visit duration, while meaningful time on page, scroll depth and conversions suggest real visitors. You can also check the Sources tab, entry pages and the Hostname filter.

question: Clicks from my www site to my shop subdomain are showing up as outbound link clicks. Can I exclude them?
reference_answer: A link counts as outbound when it leads to a different hostname, which includes your own subdomains. To leave them out, add a `transformRequest` option to your `plausible.init` call that returns null for clicks to your own domain. Clicks already recorded stay in your stats, but you can filter by the url property with does not contain and your domain.
key_facts: Different hostnames count as outbound, including your own subdomains
Use transformRequest in plausible.init to return null for your own domain
Already-recorded clicks stay in stats
answer: Yes, you can exclude clicks to your own subdomains by adding a `transformRequest` option to the `plausible.init` call in your snippet [1].
